bugs.title: Extend face-centered crop to detect animal faces
bugs.notes: Extend face-centered crop (bug-36) to animal faces; verify anime faces. FINDINGS: (1) CRITICAL pre-existing breakage — FaceCenterEngine.analyze was dead code: it sat at module level (dedented out of the class) after _load_anime_cascades, so engine.analyze() always raised AttributeError, was caught by plan_scenes' try/except, and EVERY scene silently fell back to the safe centre crop — neither human, anime, nor animal centering was actually running. (2) The bug-36 'anime' fallback looked up lbpcascade_animeface.xml inside cv2.data.haarcascades, but opencv-python-headless does NOT ship that file (verified on 5.0 and 4.10 installs), so it silently degraded to haarcascade_frontalface_default (human-only). FIX (f2ecafd): analyze() restored as a proper method; cascades loaded once in __init__; lbpcascade_animeface.xml (nagadomi, MIT) vendored into pipeline/stage_b/cascades/ and looked up there first; animal faces via OpenCV's shipped haarcascade_frontalcatface[_extended] plus a lazy YOLOv8n fallback (new optional ultralytics>=8.2,<9 dep) covering COCO animal classes (bird/cat/dog/horse/sheep/cow/elephant/bear/zebra/giraffe), detections filtered to animal classes at conf>=0.4. All tiers best-effort: any failure keeps the safe centred crop, render never fails. VERIFIED: vendored cascade loads and haar cascade detects a real face (Lena) under OpenCV 4.10 (CI version); stubbed-YOLO tests confirm animal-class filtering, confidence gating, correct normalized centres, and ultralytics-absent path returning []. 7 new ReframeDetectionTierTests; 48/48 stage_b tests pass; full pipeline suite 267 pass with only 3 pre-existing failures (confirmed identical on the pre-change base commit). HONEST LIMITS: no real anime/cat/dog image was downloadable in the sandbox, so real-photo cascade/YOLO recall is assumed from the upstream models (anime cascade params match the author's detect.py exactly); first CI run will auto-download yolov8n.pt (~6MB) at predict time — if the runner has no egress to that host, the tier logs a warning and falls through harmlessly.

bugs.title: Multi-file music upload (bug-28) not actually applying
bugs.notes: Multi-file music upload (bug-28) not actually applying. ROOT CAUSE: bug-28's 'done' status did NOT reflect working code — the current handleMusicUploadMessage uploaded the FIRST audio file immediately and then called clearFlow(), ending the music_upload flow after exactly one file; every subsequent file fell out of the flow and was silently dropped. The upload prompt (ml:upload) also had NO Done button at all, only Cancel — the batch behavior the update_notice.json changelog advertised was never shipped. FIX (75ce07e, bot/src/index.js): ml:upload now seeds state.pending.uploaded=[] and renders a prompt with an explicit 'Done' button (ml:uploaddone); handleMusicUploadMessage STAGES each file as {name, file_id} in the KV flow state (kept alive, running count shown, same filename re-sent = latest wins) instead of uploading+exiting; ml:uploaddone drains the staged list — downloads each file from Telegram and commits it to audio-library/ via putBinaryFile, reports per-file added/failed, then clearFlow + library re-render. Also fixed: Cancel (set:music) now clears a live music_upload flow so a cancelled session cannot keep swallowing audio files. VERIFIED: node --check clean; 93/93 bot tests pass; staging state machine simulated in Node (collects N files, dedupes latest-wins, Done drains all). LIMITS: index.js internals are not exported so no direct unit test of the handlers exists (consistent with the existing suite, which only tests exported modules); end-to-end Telegram behavior assumed from the flow routing in handleMessage. NOTE: file_ids are fetched at Done time and expire ~1h after send — a user who waits longer would get per-file failure messages, which the handler now reports instead of crashing.

bugs.title: Workflow dispatch must relay back to bot as the FIRST step
bugs.notes: Workflow dispatch must relay back to bot as the FIRST step. FINDINGS: the bot learns a run started by polling jobs/<id>/status.json, but the earliest status write sat at step ~7 in both stage-a.yml ('Write initial status (stage_a_running)') and stage-b.yml ('Write stage_b_running status') — behind Python setup, ffmpeg and pip dependency installation (minutes). bug-26/bug-35 only added bot/UI-layer acks (spinner, dispatch ack) and never moved the workflow-side signal earlier — confirming the suspicion in the report. FIX (e396f3c): added a 'Notify bot that the run started (first step)' step to BOTH stage-a.yml and stage-b.yml, placed immediately after checkout + HEAD re-attach (the only prerequisites for committing status) and BEFORE Set up Python / any install / processing. It writes status.json via pipeline/status.py (verified stdlib-only — runs with no setup) with state stage_a_running/stage_b_running + run id/URL + code-ref, commits and pushes with the same 3-attempt rebase-retry pattern the existing status steps use, and is continue-on-error so a notification failure can never fail the real job. --mode is deliberately omitted on the early write (write_status merges; prior mode preserved — verified locally). SCOPE AUDIT: stage-a.yml covers fresh runs, Stage A restarts, and series continuations (all dispatch the same workflow); stage-b.yml covers renders and Stage B restarts. publish.yml intentionally NOT changed — it is not a job-lifecycle workflow: its dispatches write publishing.status (not job state), 'discover' has no job_id at all, and its first meaningful step is its existing request/secret validation; telegram-relay.yml hands off to a Stage A run which now self-notifies; cleanup/diagnostics are not bot-dispatched job runners. VERIFIED: both YAML files parse; step positions confirmed (stage-a index 2, stage-b index 3); the exact CLI invocation was simulated locally incl. the bug-13/15 terminal->running restart guard (passes). LIMIT: not exercised in a real Actions run — the pre-existing later status steps remain as the authoritative fallback.
